messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty SEV2 triggered for region az-west-3 — control-plane NTP drift + NIC errors leading to connection resets on serving nodes. Alert: 5xx spike and increased tail latency for 'redwood-open-13b' across az-west-3. PD incident id: PD-89124

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty page fired to on-call (jonah). Auto-escalation in 5m if no ack.

jonah: acked. I'm on it — grabbing logs and checking routing. who's on infra? @priya can you confirm any fabric maintenance?

priya: not scheduled. seeing NIC errs in telemetry for az-west-3-az2, RX/TX errors up ~18% starting ~08:02 UTC. KVM host churn looks low.

maya: jumping in — I see increased 502/504 from the edge LB to model-pool nodes, perflow shows conn resets and TLS retries.

oliver: copying net team. @lucas is there a routing diversion we can flip from platform?

lucas: we can divert new traffic to az-west-4 and az-east-1 via the smart-router policy. Doing a quick dry-run of the policy change. Will coordinate with maya for canary shift.

maya: +1. Let's keep 10% to az-west-3 for telemetry. If error rate stabilizes, we can hold. If not, full divert.

jonah: running quick health checks:
```
# check serving node health
curl -sS http://10.12.4.23:8080/healthz | jq .
# query KV cache hit rates
redis-cli -h kvcache-az-west-3 INFO keyspace
```
Results: some nodes failing health probes (503). KV hit rates look ok.

incident-bot: Auto-escalation timer 03:10 remaining.

priya: I SSHed into a host and saw NIC errors at dmesg: 
```
link reset detected on eth0
RX desc errors: 1324
```
I'm opening a ticket with cloud provider for port-level flapping.

sara: any customer impact? CX reports?

maya: early signal — errors affecting 0.8% of requests globally but concentrated to az-west-3: ~35% increased error rate for customers routed there. A/B customers using dedicated pools in that AZ see higher latency. No major drop in requests overall.

jonah: ok let's execute lucas' diversion. lucas, note the canary plan: 10% -> 40% -> 100% over 6 minutes, measure 5xx and p50/p99. Keep 10% to az-west-3 during canary.

lucas: starting canary. Applying policy change:
```
api call: POST /router/policies/divert
payload: {"from":"az-west-3","to":["az-west-4","az-east-1"],"weights":[0.5,0.5],"canary":true}
```
Canary step 1 -> 40% new traffic diverted.

maya: monitoring: p50 stable, p99 improving slightly, 5xx down 60% in diverted pool. Keeping watch on KV cache miss rate.

incident-bot: PD auto-escalation suppressed because incident acknowledged.

priya: cloud ticket created: #CL-77821. Provider acknowledges port flapping on TOR switch for az-west-3 rack group 12. They propose moving instances to alternate NICs, ETA ~18m.

oliver: suggest we proactively drain affected serving instances to reduce user impact until provider fix.

jonah: agree. maya, can you drain and mark the nodes as in-maint? Use graceful connection drain.

maya: draining nodes now: `platform drain --region az-west-3 --pool model-pool-redwood-open-13b --grace 30s`

...drain started, 12/48 nodes removed from LB rotation. Errors continue to trend down.

sara: I'll open a quick Ops->CS blurb: short note that some customers in az-west-3 may have seen transient errors, teams investigating, following up with postmortem.

lucas: canary move to 100% diversion in 4m if signals hold.

jonah: agree. prepping a brief timeline for PD and execs.

pagerduty-bot: Notification: escalation to engineering lead in 6m if major regressions.

maya: provider update: They've migrated NICs for 3 hosts and report link flaps reduced. Observability shows further drop.

oliver: any action for Dedicated customers pinned to az-west-3?

lucas: For dedicated customers we submitted soft migrations; ops-consent required. For now, we will keep routing but escalate account managers for manual outreach.

jonah: decision: keep diversion active until provider confirms full restoration. PD incident remains SEV2. Assigning owners: maya (mitigation), priya (infra interface), lucas (routing), sara (communications).

incident-bot: Note: post-incident survey scheduled in 24h.

maya: provider confirms all switches healthy, no RX/TX errors for last 4m. rolling re-enable: gradually bring drained nodes back in 20% increments.

lucas: reverting diversion: 100% -> gradual 80/20 -> full back to az-west-3 in 10m window.

jonah: closing loop — error rate back to baseline, p99 latency normalized. PD incident set to "resolved" but keeping thread for postmortem notes.

sara: posted CS note to #customer-impact and sent Affected list to AMs: small set of orgs with dedicated pools in az-west-3. No SLA hits detected.

priya: provider ticket closed: root cause NIC firmware bug triggered under microburst load—they rolled a fix to TOR and swapped NICs.

jonah: thanks all. follow-ups for postmortem: (1) validate router fallback timeouts, (2) improve detection for NIC port flaps, (3) run tabletop for dedicated pool migrations. I'll create PM and link to this thread. :thumbsup:

oliver: thanks — nice quick coordination.

incident-bot: Thread archived to incidents with tags [az-west-3, network, SEV2, routing-divert, postmortem-required].
